Statistics and Operations Research, University of Granada</li></ul></div></div></div><div><div class="profile-name" role="heading" aria-level="1">Gustavo Rivas Gervilla</div><p class="profile-bio">He is a researcher at the University of Granada, where he has carried out his entire academic and research career. He holds degrees in Computer Engineering and Mathematics, and Master’s degrees in Computer Engineering and in Applied Statistics, and completed the Doctoral Programme in Information and Communication Technologies, all at the University of Granada.</p><p class="profile-bio">He began his research career during his doctoral studies at the Department of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence (DECSAI), and he is currently an Assistant Professor in the Department of Statistics and Operations Research. His teaching focuses on Statistical Inference and Biostatistics.</p><p class="profile-bio">His first line of research centres on fuzzy logic, formal concept analysis and natural language generation. Within this line he defended his doctoral thesis on formal mechanisms for the representation and extraction of referring expressions in data-to-text systems.</p><p class="profile-bio">His new doctoral project lies in the field of causal inference, which he began working on with <a href="../miguel-luque/index.html">Miguel Ángel Luque Fernández</a>, his current thesis supervisor, during his Master’s thesis in the Master’s in Applied Statistics. The problem he addresses is multicausality: how to make inference about an observed effect when several causes, interacting in ways that differ in nature and complexity, may combine to produce it. This is an open and demanding problem, both from the perspective of theoretical and mathematical formalisation and from that of practical applicability.</p><p class="profile-bio">He works with R, Python and higher-performance languages such as C++, and is currently learning Rust as well as web and mobile development. He is also a keen LaTeX enthusiast with an advanced command of the tool.</p></div></section><div class="profile-related-surface"><svg class="profile-wave profile-wave-top" viewBox="0 0 1440 80" preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M0 16 C280 16 420 32 700 48 C980 64 1170 64 1440 64 L1440 80 H0 Z"/></svg><section class="section wrap section-tight profile-related"><div class="section-heading"><div><h2>Related research areas</h2></div></div><article class="research-area-detail" id="research-complex-treatments" role="region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="research-complex-treatments-title"><div class="research-visual"><img src="../../assets/line-complex.svg?v=6" alt="" width="300" height="150" loading="lazy"></div><div class="research-area-copy"><h3 id="research-complex-treatments-title">Causal estimation with complex exposures</h3><div class="research-area-body"><p>Methods for estimating causal effects of treatments with multiple levels or complex exposures within the potential outcomes framework. We combine doubly robust estimation, cross-fitting and influence-function-based inference, including when nuisance models are estimated with machine learning. The <a href="../../index.html#software">Software</a> section includes the <code>tmleMulti</code> implementation.</p></div></div></article></section><svg class="profile-wave profile-wave-end" viewBox="0 0 1440 80" preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M0 64 C280 64 470 64 740 48 C1010 32 1160 16 1440 16 L1440 80 H0 Z"/></svg></div></main>
